topic.subject: social
topic.title: Money and credit
topic.scope: barter and double coincidence of wants, money as medium of exchange, banks and deposits, credit, collateral, SHGs

concepts.name: Barter System and Double Coincidence of Wants

misconceptions.statement: Barter is just a primitive way of trading that happens when people don't have enough money.
misconceptions.why: Students often view history as a linear progression where older methods are simply 'inferior' versions of modern ones.
misconceptions.fix: Barter is a system of exchange requiring a double coincidence of wants, which becomes highly inefficient as the variety of goods and services in an economy increases.

probe.question: Why did societies move away from barter?
probe.wrong_answer: Because people became smarter and invented money to replace a broken system.

concepts.name: Money as a Medium of Exchange

misconceptions.statement: The value of a currency note comes from the paper or metal it is made of.
misconceptions.why: Students confuse the intrinsic value of a commodity (like gold) with the face value of fiat currency.
misconceptions.fix: Modern money has no intrinsic value; it is accepted as a medium of exchange because it is authorized by the government of the country.

probe.question: Why is a 500 rupee note worth more than a piece of paper of the same size?
probe.wrong_answer: Because the paper used for the note is very expensive and high quality.

misconceptions.statement: Banks keep all the money deposited by people in a safe vault until they come to withdraw it.
misconceptions.why: The common-sense view of a 'bank' is a place where money is stored, similar to a piggy bank.
misconceptions.fix: Banks keep only a small proportion of deposits as cash and use the majority of the money to extend loans to borrowers.

probe.question: What happens to the money you deposit in a bank?
probe.wrong_answer: It stays in my personal locker inside the bank until I need it.

misconceptions.statement: Taking a loan is always bad because it creates debt.
misconceptions.why: Students often hear negative stories about debt traps and fail to distinguish between productive and unproductive credit.
misconceptions.fix: Credit can be beneficial if it is used for productive purposes, such as investing in a business or farming, which helps increase income.

probe.question: Is it always a mistake for a farmer to take a loan?
probe.wrong_answer: Yes, because loans always lead to poverty and debt traps.
